h: Riverside walks and a town full of history
p: Allow an hour and a half to two hours for the castle, then head out to explore a town that punches well above its weight.

Start with the river. The Swale tumbles over a series of wide rocky steps known as Richmond Falls, just below the castle, and it's a lovely place for a paddle on a warm day, though do keep a close eye on children, as the water can rise quickly after rain. From here, a riverside walk of around a mile takes you to Easby Abbey, the atmospheric ruins of a medieval abbey, also looked after by English Heritage and free to wander. It's a gorgeous, easy stroll.

Back in the cobbled market place, the Green Howards Museum is housed in the old Holy Trinity church and tells the story of the famous Yorkshire regiment. The Richmondshire Museum is another good stop for local history. Theatre fans should look out for the Georgian Theatre Royal, built in 1788 and still putting on shows today. Tours give a fascinating glimpse behind the scenes.
Over the river, the old railway station has been turned into The Station, a community hub with cafés, a cinema and food producers. It's a handy spot for lunch.

With a car, you can head up Swaledale towards Reeth for some of the finest scenery in the Yorkshire Dales. Stone barns, drystone walls and rolling green fells make it a perfect drive after a morning of history.
